title: General Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. — This Order requires all franchise payments by jurisdictional utilities to be line-itemed on a customer's bill and finds that any franchise payment above 5% is a violation of the Commission's Promotional Practice General Order.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                              GENERAL ORDER NO. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)

                    LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, EX PARTE.

Docket No. R-37943, In re: Possible modifications to General Order dated October 12, 2007 related to
franchise fees.

                     (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


OVERVIEW & PROCEDURAL HISTORY

        This Docket was initiated by a Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”)

directive at its May 13, 2026 Business and Executive Session (“B&E”), which directed Staff to review

and possibly modify the Commission’s General Order dated October 12, 2007 related to franchise fees,

with a focus on including all franchise fees in a line-item on utility bills. Notice of this proceeding was

published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin dated June 5, 2026 with Cleco Power LLC, (“Cleco

Power”), Southwest Louisiana Electric Membership Corporation (“SLEMCO”), Pointe Coupee Electric

Membership Corporation (“PCME”), the Association of Louisiana Electric Cooperatives, Inc., (“ALEC”),

Entergy Louisiana, LLC, (“ELL”), Delta North Louisiana Gas Company, LLC., Delta South Louisiana

Gas Company, LLC, Delta Capital Gas Company, LLC, (collectively “Delta Utilities”), and Northeast

Louisiana Power Cooperative, Inc., (“NELPCO”) all timely intervening.

        A review of the transcript from the May 2026 B&E provides additional context around the

Commission’s directive and the purpose behind this rulemaking proceeding. Specifically, Chairman

Skrmetta stated:

                 “[T]he concept is we would reorient the 2008 [sic] action to where we would
                 establish all franchise action by parishes are line itemed on the bills whether
                 they be electric, gas, water, … that they are established outside of the
                 Commission authorized rates. The Commission works very hard to keep the
                 rates as low as they can be, and so they should not be interpreted as a
                 Commission rate increase. So, they should be line itemed as the particular
                 parish action for their counsel [sic] and that realistically it should be listed
                 as a tax.”1

        Staff filed its Notice of Proposed Rule and Recommendation on September 4, 2026 (“Proposed

Rules”), which largely tracked the Commission’s 19882 and 20063 General Orders, but also included the

addition of definitions as well as general Commission policies regarding utility tariffs and record keeping.

Staff sought comments on the Proposed Rules from all intervenors by September 25, 2026, in order to

2
  General Order dated October 18, 1988; LPSC, ex parte In re: Charges and other assessments not related to a utility
company’s cost of service shall appear on customer bills as a line item entry. (“1988 General Order”)
3
  Docket No. R-27859, LPSC, ex parte. In re: Amendments to the Commission’s General Order of October 18, 1988 in order
to address franchise right agreements and franchise fees.
                                                                          General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)

 have final rules proposed for Commission consideration at the Commission’s October 2026 B&E.

Comments were timely filed by ALEC, Delta Utilities, Cleco Power, ELL, and SLEMCO. Generally, all

comments were receptive to Staff’s Proposed Rules with each intervenor having requests for clarifications

or modifications to the Proposed Rules to fit certain situations.

       ALEC and ELL both focused mostly on Section 501 of the Proposed Rules and the prohibition of

recovery from customers of any franchise fee in excess of five percent. Each utility questioned the need

for this prohibition and suggested, as written, the five percent could have unintended consequences. The

Proposed Rules, specifically Section 501(B), provided that any amount of a Franchise Payment exceeding

five percent cannot be recovered by a utility via a line-item on customer’s bills, nor through base rates,

but must instead be recovered from the utility’s shareholders, investors, company margins, etc. Delta

Utilities and Cleco Power provided comments, for different reasons, regarding compliance with the

Proposed Rules, specifically the implementation of any new rule approved through this rulemaking. For

different reasons, both utilities had concerns with the Proposed Rules’ 60-day implementation deadline,

and the ability to ensure compliance with the same. SLEMCO provided one comment that was not raised

by any other intervenor, indicating SLEMCO could not support the proposed rule if applied retroactively

given how SLEMCO has structured its current franchise agreements. SLEMCO’s position was due to its

numerous franchise agreements which provide that one-half of the franchise fee is recovered as a line item

charge on customer bills and the remaining one-half is recovered in SLEMCO’s base rates.

       After considering all the comments received, Staff filed Staff’s Notice of Final Rule and

Recommendation (“Final Proposed Rules”) on October 5, 2026, which were considered at the October 22,

2026 Business and Executive Session, and are attached hereto as Attachment A.

COMMISSION JURISDICTION

       Article IV, Section 21 (B) of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974 grants the LPSC constitutional

jurisdiction over common carriers, and specifically provides as follows:

               “The [public service] commission shall regulate all common carriers and
               public utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
               It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures
               necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have other powers and
               perform other duties as provided by law.”

The Louisiana Supreme Court has repeatedly held that the above-referenced provision gives the

Commission exclusive, plenary power to regulate all common carriers and public utilities.       Louisiana

Power & Light Co. v. LPSC, 609 So.2d 797, 800 (La. 1992); Bowie v. LPSC, 627 So.2d 164, 166 (La.

1993); Entergy Gulf States, Inc. v. LPSC, 1998-0881 (La. 1/20/99), 726 So.2d 870, 873.                The

Commission’s power is as complete in every respect as the regulatory power that would have been vested
                                                                    General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                   Page 2
 in the legislature absent Article IV, Section 21. Consequently, “the Commission is vested explicitly and

implicitly with the constitutional power necessary to the performance of its function of regulating common

carriers and public utilities through the adoption and enforcement of reasonable rules and orders requisite

to these purposes.” Louisiana Consumers’ League Inc. v. LPSC, 351 So.2d 128, 131 (La. 1977); Central

Louisiana Electric Co. v. LPSC, 373 So. 2d 123, 128 (La. 1979); South Central Bell Telephone Co. v.

LPSC, 412 So. 2d 1069, 1070 (La. 1982).

        As part of the Commission’s regulatory authority, the Commission has exclusive jurisdiction in

setting just and reasonable rates to be charged by a jurisdictional utility. Daily Advertiser, 612 So. 2d 7,

16 (La. 1/19/93) citing Gulf States Utilities Co. v. LPSC, 578 So.2d 71, 100 (La. 1992), cert. denied, 502

U.S. 1004, 112 S.Ct. 637, 116 L.Ed. 2d 655 (1991). In setting just and reasonable rates, the Commission

should allow a utility to recoup its revenue requirement – sufficient revenues to meet its operating

expenses, provide its shareholders with a reasonable rate of return, and attract new capital. Central

Louisiana Electric Co. v. LPSC, 508 So. 2d at 1365 (1987). In connection with that, the Commission is

required to determine how much of a utility’s investment should be included in rate base, ultimately to be

borne by the ratepayers. In doing so, the Commission balances the interest of the ratepayers in the lowest

possible rates, against that of the utility and its investors, who understandably desire the highest possible

rates. Morehouse National Gas Co. v. Louisiana Public Service Commission, 245 La. 983, 162 So.2d 334

(1964). One of the principles used by ratemaking bodies and courts to make such a determination is the prudent

investment rule. Under the prudent investment rule, a utility is compensated for all prudent investments at their

cost when made, irrespective of whether they are deemed necessary or beneficial in hindsight. Duquesne Light

Co. v. Barasch, 488 U.S. 299, 109 S.Ct. 609, 102 L.Ed.2d 646 (1989).

        In addition to the Commission’s constitutional authority, the Louisiana Legislature has established

law regarding political subdivisions of the State and allowing such to collect payments from public utilities

in certain defined situations. La. Revised Statute 33:4510 provides in pertinent part:

                (A) Whenever any political subdivision of the state of Louisiana ... shall
                collect or receive any payment from any public utility operating within such
                political subdivision, including those utilities whose rates and charges are
                regulated by the Louisiana Public Service Commission, for … the use of its
                streets, alleys, or public ways or places ... the amount of such tax or payment
                may, to the extent that such tax or payment was not included as a part of the
                cost of furnishing services in the fixing of the rates and charges for such
                services by the Louisiana Public Service Commission, be added to the sales
                price of such public utility’s service and billed pro rata to the utility’s
                customers receiving local service within the political subdivision collecting
                such taxes or receiving such payments.


                ***

                                                                      General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                         Page 3
                 (D) The provisions of this Section shall not apply to any payments by a
                utility to a political subdivision in excess of five percent of the annual gross
                receipts of the utility from its customers within said political subdivision ...

STAFF’S ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATION ON FINAL PROPOSED RULES

        The Commission initially reviewed franchise fees in 1988. As a part of that review, The

Commission detailed its concern that confusion could result as to the actual cost of utility service if utilities

were also including other charges, taxes, and/or assessments on customer’s bill without proper

identification of those charges. Ultimately, the Commission determined that it was in the public interest

for all jurisdictional utilities to describe each non-service related charge as a line item on customer bills

so the “customer can quickly verify the true amount of their utility rates.”4 The 1988 General Order

remained in place for almost twenty-years until the Commission reconsidered franchise fees and whether

such constituted a violation of the Commission’s General Order dated March 12, 1974 (“Promotional

Practices General Order”).5 The Commission determined that franchise agreements and associated fees

did not violate the Commission’s Promotional Practices General Order; however, the Commission

initiated Docket No. R-27859 to review the 1988 General Order, and ultimately issued 2006 General

Order, which provided further clarity surrounding the 1988 General Order, limited franchise payments to

5% or less, prohibited any franchise payments in a utility’s base rates, and required franchise payments to

be line-itemed on a pro-rata basis to utility customers. In issuing Commission General Order dated October

31, 2006 (“2006 General Order”) the Commission did not supersede the 1988 General Order, but

incorporated it therein.

         Subsequent to the 2006 General Order, the Commission directed Staff to review the 2006 General

Order based on concerns of the Louisiana Municipal Association. At the Commission’s May 2007 B&E,

the Commission determined that fifty-percent of franchise fees shall be placed in base rates, collected

from all utility customers, with the remaining fifty-percent borne by the customers located within the

municipality charging said franchise fees and noted as a line item on customer bills. The Commission’s

action was memorialized in Commission General Order dated October 12, 2007 (“2007 General Order”).

There have been no additional amendments to the Commission’s rules associated with franchise

agreements and their respective payments since the 2007 General Order.

        Based on the Commission’s directive and the discussion had at the May 2026 B&E, Staff started

its analysis with a review of the 2006 General Order and determined minimal modifications or



4
 See 1988 General Order.
5
 Docket No. R-26966, LPSC, ex parte, In re: Commission consideration of whether or not the Commission’s General Order
of March 12, 1974 (Re: Promotional Practices) needs to be amended to exclude these practices with respect to franchise
agreements.
                                                                          General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                              Page 4
 clarifications were necessary as the intent – providing uniformity amongst jurisdictional utilities for non-

service related charges – remains in the public interest. Furthermore, the intent of the 1988 General Order

– ensuring customers have transparency on their utility bill, including knowing their utility rate – also

remains in the public interest. Staff took the position that franchise fees are not a part of a utility’s cost of

service as they do not meet the general definition of operating expenses and are not related to, and arguably

not necessary for, regulated operations. A utility’s revenue requirement is set by establishing sufficient

revenues to meet the utility’s operating expenses, provide its shareholders with a reasonable rate of return,

and attract new capital. Central Louisiana Electric Co., supra. Generally speaking, operating expenses

include maintenance, depreciation and taxes incurred. Entergy Gulf States, Inc. v. LPSC, 98-1235 (La.

4/16/199), 730 So.2d 890, 895. By their very definition, franchise agreements and fees associated

therewith are discretionary, and unregulated by the Commission.6 Expenses not related to regulated

operations should be excluded from base rates of a utility. Id. As such, based upon the precedent cited

above, as well as the comments in support of Staff’s Proposed Rules, Staff maintained, in the Final

Proposed Rules that the Commission only allow prudently incurred costs to provide regulated services to

be included within base rates.

        Staff recognized the distinction between the Commission’s jurisdiction (rate-setting authority over

utilities and common carriers) and a political subdivision’s ability to negotiate franchise agreements and

associated fees, including with a public utility, and reiterated in the Final Proposed Rules that this

rulemaking does not alter a political subdivision’s ability related to franchise agreements and associated

fees. As such, the Commission does not take a position on a public utility entering into a franchise

agreement, nor the fee a public utility may pay associated with a franchise agreement. However, the

Commission does take interest in whether, and to what extent, any fees associated with franchise

agreements are appropriately recovered by public utilities and their customers. As such, Staff

recommended the Commission find that any payment for franchise fees above five percent be considered

a payment for the purpose of enticing a utility subscriber to take service in preference to service of another

public utility in violation of the Commission’s Promotional Practices General Order. In Staff’s

recommendation, a utility paying more than 5% in franchise payments was the equivalent of enticing a

service user to select one utility over another for services rendered, which is a violation of the

Commission’s Promotional Practices General Order.




6

and public places therein, … (emphasis added).
                                                                              General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                                     Page 5
 COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

              This matter was considered at the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive

Session. After discussion, on motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, and

unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to adopt the Final Rules filed into the record on October 5,

2026, with amendments. Vice Chairman Coussan’s motion was to adopt the Final Rules with an

amendment to Section 601 to read as follows:

Notwithstanding the foregoing:

       (i)       Any jurisdictional utility with a rate proceeding pending before or prescribed by the
                 Commission as of the effective date of this Order shall comply with the requirements of this
                 Order upon the effective date of new rates resulting from such proceedings; and,

       (ii)      Any jurisdictional utility that is a party to an existing contract for Franchise Payments with a
                 Political Subdivision that is currently billed in compliance with the Commission’s 2007 Order
                 shall comply with the requirements of this Order and when contract amendments can be
                 negotiated with said Political Subdivisions, but in no event later than the renewal of existing
                 contracts for Franchise Payments which may only be executed in compliance with this Order
                 and as the same may be amended from time to time.7


IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

              1) The Commission’s adopts Staff’s Final Rules filed into the record on October 5, 2026, with
                 the modifications read into the record at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive
                 Session, and attached hereto as Attachment A.

              2) This order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA

FRANCHISE AGREMENTS AND ASSOCIATED FEES

                   LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
     RULES REGARDING FRANCHISE AGREEMENTS AND ASSOCIATED FEES


                                             PURPOSE

       The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission” or “LPSC”) hereby promulgates the
following rules (the “Rules”) in an effort to affirm rules applicable to all public utilities subject to the
jurisdiction of the Commission. These Rules are intended to ensure public utilities line-item certain
charges on utility bills in lieu of rolling those costs into base rates. Furthermore, these Rules also clarify
that line-item charges for Franchise Payments are not in violation of the Commission’s General Order
dated April 7, 2004 on prohibited promotional practices.
       Consequently, the Commission finds it necessary to affirm these Rules to require public utilities
to not only line-item certain charges, but to also provide a description of such charges to ensure Customers
understand their utility bill and can quickly verify the true amount of their utility rate.
                                               AUTHORITY

       Article IV, Section 21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974 provides the Commission with the
following authority:

       B.      Powers and Duties. The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and
       public utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by Law. It shall adopt
       and enforce reasonable rules, regulations and procedures necessary for the discharge of its
       duties, and shall have other powers and perform other duties as provided by Law.

       Consistent with the above authority, the Commission has adopted rules and regulations that apply

to utilities in general, and in some cases a specific class(es) of utilities. The blanket authority to regulate

public utilities granted above, however, is not absolute, as it is subject to the following limitations

regarding utilities owned, operated or regulated by a political subdivision:


       C.     Limitation. The Commission shall have no power to regulate any common carrier
       or public utility owned, operated, or regulated on the effective date of this constitution by
       the governing authority of one or more political subdivisions, except by the approval of a
       majority of the electors voting in an election held for that purpose; however, a political
       subdivision may reinvest itself with such regulatory power in the manner in which it was
       surrendered. This paragraph shall not apply to safety regulations pertaining to the
       operation of such utilities.

       It is consistent with the above-cited Constitutional authority that the Commission adopts these

Rules that are intended to apply to all Commission-jurisdictional public utilities.

SECTION 101. Definitions

1. Customer- A (i) natural person or (ii) a single juridical entity, including any of its affiliated companies
   which are affiliated through common ownership, who receive, and pay for, Service from a
   jurisdictional Public Utility.

2. Franchise Payment – Any payment whether it be called a license, privilege, or franchise, inspection or
   occupational tax, charge, or fee, or otherwise, provided to a political subdivision by a jurisdictional
   utility in exchange for the utility’s use of the political subdivision’s streets, alleys, or public ways or
   places, or for or by reason of the operation of the utility’s business within the political subdivision.
                                                                      General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                       Page 8
 3. Municipality – An incorporated city, town, or village.

4. Political Subdivision- A parish, municipality, and any other unit of local government, including a
   school board and a special district authorized by law to perform governmental functions.

5. Public Utility – Shall include electric cooperatives and public utility activity or service under the
   jurisdiction of the Commission.

6. Rate- Any compensation, charge, fare, toll, rental, or classification that is observed, charged, or
   collected by a jurisdictional public utility for a Service, product or commodity it provides as allowed
   by law.

7. Rate Rider- A Rate Rider is an additional Rate or charge to be applied to a Customer bill that is separate
   and distinct from the basic Rates paid under the Customer’s applicable Rate Schedule. Typically, Rate
   Riders are applied to more than one Rate Schedule, although that is not a requirement.

8. Rate Schedule(s) - A schedule(s) included within a jurisdictional public utility’s Tariff, which provides
   the various Rates for particular classes for which the utility anticipates offering Services under. Each
   specific Rate Schedule shall include: 1) Type of Service provided under the Schedule; 2) Rates and
   charges associated with Service under the Schedule; 3) All classification(s) of Customers which could
   be included under the Schedule; and 4) All practices, rules or regulations which specifically apply to
   the Services under the Schedule.
   There shall be no Rate Schedule(s) designed to be applicable to one Customer. This prohibition is not
   meant to contradict with the allowance of a Site-Specific Contract as provided for in Section 601 of
   Commission General Order dated July 1, 2019.

9. Service- The term Service means the sale or distribution of the jurisdictional public utility’s
   commodity in the performance of the public utility’s responsibilities.

10. Tariff-The all-encompassing document filed with, and approved by, the Commission to which all
    jurisdictional public utilities provide Service. A jurisdictional public utility’s Tariff contains rules to
    address the responsibilities and authorities of the utility as it relates to its various Customer classes.
    Such rules shall address, but are not limited to: Rates, allocation of costs for line extensions, and
    allocation of costs for new Customer connections. The Tariff shall also include other issues which
    define the responsibilities and authorities of the jurisdictional public utility.

   The Tariff shall include, but is not limited to: Rate Schedules, Rate Riders, and Terms of Service.

11. Terms of Service- Terms of Service are included within a jurisdictional public utility’s Tariff and are
    intended to facilitate the rendering of uniform, efficient and adequate Service to the various Customer
    classes of the utility. Specifically, the Terms of Service defines the responsibilities, obligation, and
    authorities the utility possesses in exchange for its provision of Service to Customers, as well as the
    responsibilities and obligations of Customers in exchange for receiving Service.

SECTION 201. Applicability

All jurisdictional utilities, including but not limited to electric, gas, telephone, sewerage and water

providers, shall describe each charge that is unrelated to the Rate Schedule or Rider for that Service to

their customers. These charges shall appear as a line item on each customer bill. Each line item shall

contain a brief description of the charge and the amount of said charge. Charges not related to an approved

Rate Schedule or Rider, include but are not limited to, those items appearing on a bill where monies

collected by a utility are remitted to a third party. Examples of these charges shall include, but are not

limited to: assessments imposed by federal, state, parish, municipal, or other local governmental authority,

franchise taxes, franchise fees, emergency 911 service, telecommunications for the deaf fund, or any
                                                                     General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                       Page 9
 payment by a utility to a Political Subdivision whether such payment be called a license, privilege,

franchise, inspection or occupational tax, charge, or fee where said charges are not included in a utility’s

approved Tariff structure.

SECTION 301. Prohibited Recovery of Charges and/or Fees

This Order prohibits the recovery of any charge that is unrelated to the Rate Schedule(s) and/or Rider(s)

for that Service to a jurisdictional utility’s customers, including Franchise Payments, from a utility’s base

rates. All monies collected by a utility and remitted to a third-party shall be appropriately line-itemed

based upon the provisions found herein.

SECTION 401. Cost Recovery for Franchise Payments

Nothing in this Order shall prohibit a jurisdictional utility from providing a Political Subdivision a

Franchise Payment as a part of obtaining franchise rights. However, in order to ensure proper allocation,

collection, and recovery of such fees, the following provisions must be followed:

       A) In conformity with La. Revised Statute 33:4510, any amount of a Franchise Payment up to 5%
          of gross receipts shall be billed pro rata to the utility’s Customers receiving local service within
          the Political Subdivision collecting or receiving such payments and contributing to the
          revenues that give rise to the Franchise Payment.

       B) With the exception of a Franchise Payment, equal to or less than 5% of gross receipts, any
          other type of offer or gathering of a payment, rebate, preference or prize, or discrimination of
          any sort, including the granting or denial of any utility Service, for the purpose of enticing,
          persuading or causing a utility subscriber or potential subscriber to deal with or take any
          Service of such public utility or any of its affiliates in preference to the service of any other
          public utility, continues to be prohibited under the Commission General Order dated April 7,
          2004 (promotional practices order).

       C) The jurisdictional utility shall be allowed to provide the Franchise Payment to the Political
          Subdivision in any fashion it so desires or that has been negotiated by it and the Political
          Subdivision. However, proper collection of the Franchise Payments is required and governed
          by Sections 501(A) and (B) above.


SECTION 501. Records, Record Keeping and Grandfather Clause

A. Commission approved Tariffs shall be maintained by the Commission, as well as the jurisdictional

   public utility. The utility must maintain a complete copy of the Tariff at the Utility’s primary office

   location, or other location as authorized by the Commission, as well as an electronic version on the

   Utility’s website - to the extent one is maintained.

B. All records that a jurisdictional public utility is required to keep, by reason of rules prescribed by the

   Commission, shall be kept at the utility’s primary office location or other location as authorized by

   the Commission. Such records shall be open for inspection by authorized representatives of the

   Commission at the utility’s primary office during normal office hours, or other location as authorized

   by the Commission. Upon request of a regulated entity or other person, any records received by the
                                                                    General Order No. 11-19-2026 (R-37943)
                                                                                                     Page 10
     Commission, which are shown by the utility, or other person, and found by the Commission to be trade

    secret, proprietary, or confidential shall be kept confidential and shall be exempt from public

    disclosure, subject to the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, Rule 12.1.

C. All records associated with a franchise agreement between a jurisdictional public utility and a Political

    Subdivision, including Franchise Payments, shall be kept by the jurisdictional public utility at the

    utility’s primary office location or other location as authorized by the Commission.

SECTION 601. Effective Date and Utility Compliance

No later than the first billing cycle which begins sixty-days from the effective date of this Order, all

Commission jurisdictional utilities shall remove all charges that are unrelated to the Rate Schedule(s)

and/or Rider(s) for that Service to a jurisdictional utility’s customers, including Franchise Payments,

currently being recovered through base rates and recover the payments as specified in this Order. The

removal of Franchise Payments can be achieved either in a rate stabilization filing, in an application for

rate balancing or similar application with the Commission, or by voluntarily adjusting its rates downward.

If rates are adjusted downward, the utility must provide written confirmation to the Commission.8 For

jurisdictional electric utilities, any filing made with the Commission shall be pursuant to Section 501(C)

of Commission General Order dated July 1, 2019.

Notwithstanding the foregoing,

    (i)      Any jurisdictional utility with a rate proceeding pending before or prescribed by the
             Commission as of the effective date of this Order shall comply with the requirements of this
             Order upon the effective date of new rates resulting from such proceeding; and

    (ii)     Any jurisdictional utility that is a party to an existing contract for Franchise Payments with a
             Political Subdivision that is currently billed in compliance with the Commission’s 2007 Order
             shall comply with the requirements of this Order. Such compliance must occur as soon as
             practicable and no later than such time as contract amendments can be negotiated with said
             Political Subdivisions, and further, in no event later than the renewal of existing contracts for
             Franchise Payments which may only be executed in compliance with this Order and as the
             same may be amended from time to time.




8
 Sections 201 - 601 herein do not require any public utility to adjust rates with respect to any Franchise Payments that are paid,
credited, or otherwise provided to a Political Subdivision pursuant to an agreement or practice in effect prior to the date such
public utility became subject to price regulation by the Commission.
